Welcome to Riftbond Basics featuring the
ground rules. Riftbond is a trading card
game based on the League of Legends
universe in which the aim is to score
eight victory points across two
different battlefields. Points are
scored by moving your own units onto one
of the battlefields and conquering it or
by holding it for more than one turn.
The different car types in Riftbound are
units, gears, and spells. To play these,
you must pay an energy cost, which is
shown in the top left corner of the
card, as well as a power cost.
Energy is obtained by exhausting runes.
These come from the 12 card rune deck
from which the top two cards are played
for free at the beginning of each turn.
If you exhaust your runes to pay energy,
you must also pay a power cost for some
cards. To do this, you simply place one
of your runes bearing the symbol shown
on the card under your rune deck. You
can also use runes that are already
exhausted for this.
The domains of the runes and the cards
you play in your main and sight deck are
determined by your legend. Units that
you play enter the board exhausted. This
means they cannot move until they are
readyed at the start of the next turn.
Just like all other exhausted cards on
your side, you initially play your units
and gears into your base. There they are
protected from combat. Gears can't get
into combat. If you already control a
battlefield, you also have the option to
play your units directly from your hand
onto it. This is where your units might
comes into play. This is the number
shown on the top right hand corner of
the units. Might represents both the
attack power and the defensive stat of
your units. If a player moves units into
an already occupied battlefield, combat
stunts. Here, spells with action and
reaction speed can be activated to deal
damage or modify might. When combat
occurs and no player wishes to activate
any more spells or abilities, the total
might of all units is added together and
distributed amongst the opposing units.
Players may decide for themselves which
opposing unit they wish to damage. Once
combat is over, any damage is healed by
units that were involved and did not
die. The game ends when a player reaches
eight victory points, though this is not
quite so easy to achieve. Whilst every
other point simply requires conquering a
battlefield to earn the eighth point,
you must either have held a battlefield
for one round or you score two points in
the same round. Now you've got all the
information you need to know to start
enjoying a game of Riftbound.
